institution: National Board of Accreditation / ABET Framework

program_outcomes.title: Engineering Knowledge
program_outcomes.description: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.

program_outcomes.title: Problem Analysis
program_outcomes.description: Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.

program_outcomes.title: Design/Development of Solutions
program_outcomes.description: Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for public health and safety, and cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.

program_outcomes.title: Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems
program_outcomes.description: Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.

program_outcomes.title: Modern Tool Usage
program_outcomes.description: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modeling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations.

program_outcomes.title: The Engineer and Society
program_outcomes.description: Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice.

program_outcomes.title: Environment and Sustainability
program_outcomes.description: Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development.

program_outcomes.title: Ethics
program_outcomes.description: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.

program_outcomes.title: Individual and Team Work
program_outcomes.description: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.

program_outcomes.title: Communication
program_outcomes.description: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large, such as being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions.

program_outcomes.title: Project Management and Finance
program_outcomes.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and management principles and apply these to one's own work, as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.

program_outcomes.title: Life-long Learning
program_outcomes.description: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.

program_specific_outcomes.title: Systems & Algorithmic Foundations
program_specific_outcomes.description: Analyze, design, and optimize complex software systems, algorithmic architectures, and computational models adhering to industry benchmarks.

program_specific_outcomes.title: Applied Intelligent & Autonomous Systems
program_specific_outcomes.description: Implement, deploy, and validate modern autonomous workflows, intelligent perception pipelines, and data-driven systems.

program_specific_outcomes.title: Ethical Engineering & Industrial Rigor
program_specific_outcomes.description: Lead multi-disciplinary engineering initiatives incorporating safety standards, algorithmic accountability, and verified institutional practices.

scale.3: Substantial / High correlation (Directly addressed through dedicated instruction, assignments, and exam assessments > 40% of CO)
scale.2: Moderate / Medium correlation (Addressed through coursework, mini-projects, or lab sessions 20% to 40% of CO)
scale.1: Slight / Low correlation (Touched upon tangentially or as prerequisite foundation < 20% of CO)

requirements: Every CO must map to at least one PO with strength 1, 2, or 3.
Each non-blank correlation must include a single-line articulation justification statement.
Laboratory components must provide substantial support (3) to PO4 (Investigation) and PO5 (Tool Usage).
Courses with ethics components must provide correlation (2 or 3) to PO8 (Ethics).
